rationale: five11 is a tiny (1259 text bytes, 12 functions) bitstream-decoder benchmark whose hot path is the five11/read_x_bits/read_11_bits decode loop dominated by cheap arithmetic and shift operations, so SUB and SPLIT get high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights since they add negligible per-iteration cost and compose well on arithmetic-heavy code, and FLA gets the highest SecurityGain with a moderate RuntimeCost weight (0.4) because flattening the decoder's control flow yields the biggest analysis hurdle while its dispatch overhead is tolerable in a loop this small; BCF is kept but with the lowest RuntimeCost (0.2) and SizeCost (0.3) weights since bogus predicates and cloned blocks are the most expensive pass and would disproportionately inflate a 1259-byte text section if applied to hot functions, restricting it to larger or colder functions; IBR and ICALL get middling weights — indirect branches/calls diversify the already-flattened control flow but this program has few call sites, limiting ICALL's payoff; IGV gets moderate weights as there are few globals to virtualize; all CorrectnessRisk weights stay >=0.6 (SUB/SPLIT at 0.9) because these transformations are semantics-preserving on straight-line bit manipulation and the small function count makes miscompilation risk low.
